issues.claim: Finding 3 headline: 'roughly a quarter of retainer clients are gone within 12 months'
issues.problem: The cited page (prometheanresearch.com/client-retention-rate/) reports that 5% of 165 agency leaders say average retainer tenure is under six months and 18% say 6-12 months, i.e. ~23% of AGENCY LEADERS report an average tenure under one year. It does not measure the share of CLIENTS lost in 12 months. The finding's own evidence field states the source wording correctly and notes the page measured tenure, not a retention rate, so the headline is an unlabelled unit change rather than a wrong figure.
issues.fix: Reword the headline to 'about a quarter of agency leaders report average retainer tenure under one year', or keep 'a quarter' but mark it as an inference from a tenure distribution, not a client-level churn rate.

issues.claim: Finding 7 evidence: 'Promethean's report likewise finds 28% of agencies use a time-and-materials plus fixed-bid plus retainer mix, and only 4% or fewer rely on any single model exclusively.'
issues.problem: Both figures are correct (Promethean PDF p.35) but the finding's source_url cites only the Ignition press release, so the Promethean half of the evidence is uncited at the finding level. Not a factual error, a citation gap.
issues.fix: Add the Promethean PDF URL to finding 7's source_url (or split it into two findings), since the 28% coincidence across two surveys is doing real work in the finding.

issues.claim: Finding 16 title: 'Demand exists for small, ringfenced AI engagements rather than large transformations.'
issues.problem: The Source Global page supports the small-scope numbers (66% small-scale testing, 54% limited-scope) but also reports 71% have worked with consultants on a large project with a well-defined goal and 47% on large transformational projects, so 'rather than large transformations' overstates the tilt. The 71% is disclosed in the evidence field, so this is a framing issue, not a missing number.
issues.fix: Soften to 'demand exists for small, ringfenced engagements alongside large, well-defined ones' or mark the comparison as the consultant's reading of the page.

claims_checked.claim: Agency Core: 778 agency leaders, fielded 13 Nov-31 Dec 2024, margin of error +/-3.4 points
68% of agencies lost clients in the last year, up from 56% in 2023; 24% cite client defection risk as a severe challenge vs 11% in 2023; fewer than half have formal anti-defection programmes
Only 7% of leaders say their agency is extremely effective at growing existing-client spend; 15% of the Loyalty Builders segment say they are very effective
Report is free and ungated; states 'No gates. No gimmicks. Just the data agency leaders need, completely free'
57% of agencies lose $1,000-$5,000 a month on unbilled work; 30% say scope creep costs more than $5,000 a month; 78% rarely or only sometimes charge for out-of-scope work

Only 16% of agencies require full payment upfront, 49% request partial payment in advance; 71% say at least one in four invoices is paid late; 56% say late invoices take 2 weeks to 2 months past due; 84% spend 3-10+ hours a month chasing late payments
Ignition pricing models: 28% hourly as majority model, 28% productised/subscription/tiered, 25% project-based, 10% retainer; survey of 273 agency managers and executives

Among 165 agency leaders, 42% report average retainer tenure above two years, 30% above three years, 5% under six months, 18% 6-12 months; page states respondents were asked tenure, not to compute a retention rate

62% say onboarding access delays hurt client confidence and 60% say delays damage the relationship; agencies with formal onboarding, QBRs, dedicated account managers and agreed KPIs retain longer; referral clients stayed 1.9x longer than events/networking/outbound clients

Fixed-fee/project pricing carries 'the bulk of the risk of these engagements ... with the agency, as scoping inaccuracies can easily erode margins'; most appropriate where scopes are predictable and well-defined
2024 average agency net margin 14% against roughly 16% average over 2015-2024

84% of agencies identify as specialists (77% by service mix, 57% by industry); specialists 'consistently grow faster than generalists' and grew 43% faster than average in 2024; specialists are harder to replace so clients stick longer
Fast-growing agencies completed 24% more projects while serving 16% fewer retainer clients than average

Promethean report: 28% use a T&M + fixed-bid + retainer mix and 4% or fewer rely on any single model exclusively; 55 pages; 1,062 agency respondents from 2015-2025 surveys; sample skews to larger agencies; reuse permitted with attribution

ScalePad MSP churn distribution: 11% no churn, 45% 1-5%, 27% 6-10%, 12% 11-20%, 3% 21%+, 2% don't know; churn is top growth challenge for 26%; only 35% track client churn; 60% have formal Customer Success programmes
Lower-churn MSPs more likely to use structured onboarding, formal account management, monthly/quarterly QBRs and 1-2+ year roadmaps; page publishes no sample size, fieldwork dates or methodology
MSPs with best-in-class CSAT are more likely to report either almost no churn or higher-than-average churn, because buying decisions sit with senior stakeholders not answering ticket surveys

JumpCloud: 28% too expensive, 26% outgrown MSP, 23% poor customer service/account team, 21% offered more than needed, 18% products no longer supported, 16% felt too small; 76% rely on an MSP for at least some functions; 67% plan to increase MSP investment

Vertical SaaS benchmark: median GRR 90% multi-product vs 92% single-product; NRR 110% vs 105%; text says churn is tied to Control Point stickiness rather than product breadth and that single-product NRR hovers near/below 100% unless prices rise; more than 200 companies surveyed

MIT NANDA: 300+ public AI initiatives reviewed, 52 organisation interviews, 153 senior-leader survey responses; for custom/task-specific GenAI 60% evaluated, 20% piloted, 5% reached production; 95% of organisations report zero return; top mid-market performers ~90 days pilot-to-implementation vs 9+ months for enterprises; external partnerships twice the internal-build success rate; buyer priorities trust/workflow understanding/minimal disruption/data boundaries/improvement over time

SBE Council: 532 owners of firms with 2-99 employees, fielded 12-19 March 2025, credibility interval +/-4.3; 58% actively deploying AI; median annual AI spend just under $1,000; 96% of deployers will continue investing; 70% plan to increase spend

Source Global: 81% of clients paid for AI consulting support in the past 12 months; 99% expect to use AI advisors; 66% used small-scale support to test potential; 54% bought a limited-scope project; 71% worked on a large project with a well-defined goal; informal unpaid discussions a small slice

Skcript: USD 7,500 US fixed 10-day pilot; check-ups from USD 4,000; 4-6 week rollout priced after the pilot; 50% upfront on check-ups and pilots with rollouts billed in stages; check-up fee counts toward pilot and pilot fee toward rollout if started within 30 days; monthly care with three-month minimum, optional, unpriced; quote 'Open-ended discovery phases are where budgets disappear'

NJSBDC: 100+ staff and consultants, seven regional centers at public colleges/universities, state office at Rutgers Business School Newark, eRFC required before consulting, 'Nearly all of our services are provided at no cost through funding from federal, state, and local grants'
